title: Troupe config.yaml, version 1
description: The user's config.yaml, a project's .troupe/config.yaml and .troupe/config.local.yaml. Generated from Troupe.Config.Schema by mix troupe.config.schema; do not edit.

version.description: The version of this format. A file without it is version 1.

$schema.description: Where an editor finds this schema. Troupe does not read it.

provider.description: The session-wide provider's API. Read from a project's file only in a trusted workspace.

base_url.description: The session-wide provider's URL. Unset: the vendor's own endpoint. Read from a project's file only in a trusted workspace.

api_key.description: The session-wide provider's key. `{env:VAR}` reads it from the environment. Read from a project's file only in a trusted workspace.

auth.description: How the key is sent: the vendor's own header, or `Authorization: Bearer`. Read from a project's file only in a trusted workspace.

providers.description: Named providers. A model spelled `<provider>/<model>` goes to that provider. Read from a project's file only in a trusted workspace.

type.description: The API it speaks. A gateway such as LiteLLM or vLLM is `openai`.

base_url.description: Where it is. Unset: the vendor's own endpoint.

api_key.description: Its key. `{env:VAR}` reads it from the environment.

auth.description: How the key is sent: the vendor's own header, or `Authorization: Bearer`.

models.description: The models it serves, by the name Troupe addresses them with.

id.description: The id that goes on the wire, when the gateway renamed the model. Unset: the name.

context.description: The model's context window, in tokens.

max_output.description: The most output tokens to ask for.

reasoning_effort.description: How hard the model should think: `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`, or a thinking budget in tokens. An Anthropic model gets it in the form it takes.

auth_token.description: Old spelling of api_key with auth: bearer.

default.description: The model every agent uses unless its definition names one. A bare id goes to the session-wide provider; `<provider>/<model>` goes to a named one, from `providers` or opencode. `troupe models` lists what this machine can address.

cheap.description: The model for small jobs, compaction summaries among them. Unset: the default model.

expensive.description: The model an agent asking for `expensive` gets. Unset: the default model.

windows.description: Context windows for bare model ids, in tokens.

prices.description: Prices for models the provider's catalog does not price, by the name a model is addressed with. What a gateway says a call cost still wins, then the catalog's price.

cache_read.description: Dollars per million prompt tokens read from the cache. Unset: the input price.

cache_write.description: Dollars per million prompt tokens written to the cache. Unset: the input price.

max_tokens.description: The most output tokens one model call asks for.

context_window.description: The window, in tokens, assumed when neither a provider nor the catalog says; compaction is planned against it.

compact_at.description: The share of the window at which an agent summarises older turns. A tool result over 16 KiB it read before then is sent from then on as a stub `read_output` expands.

llm_timeout_ms.description: How long one model call may take before it is given up on.

identify.description: Every model call names Troupe: a User-Agent with the version and the client, LiteLLM's tags and the session's id to a gateway, OpenRouter's app headers to OpenRouter; never a person, a path or a repository. `false` sends none of it. `troupe doctor` prints what goes out. Read from a project's file only in a trusted workspace.

thinking_binding.description: An experiment, Anthropic only: `drop_block` sends the `thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01` beta and asks the API to drop a thinking block whose conversation changed since it was made, instead of refusing the call.

system_prompt.description: An experiment: `stable` keeps the system prompt the same for the whole session, and sends the instruction files, the brief, the goal and the task list with the turn instead, each again only when it changed.

max_turns.description: Model calls an agent may make before its budget stops it.

max_input_tokens.description: Input tokens an agent may spend.

max_output_tokens.description: Output tokens an agent may spend.

wall_clock_ms.description: How long an agent may run.

max_depth.description: How deep agents may delegate; 1 means the root alone may.

budget_warn_at.description: The share of any limit at which the agent is warned.

full_send.description: No budget warnings: an agent nearing a limit says nothing until the limit stops it. `troupe --full-send` sets it for one run.

budget_asks.description: A spent budget asks the person attached, rather than stopping.

auto_approve.description: Run every tool call without asking. Off, a write, an edit or a shell command waits until a person allows it, once or for the rest of the session, or denies it. Read from a project's file only in a trusted workspace.

approvals.description: What a call that asks does with nobody attached: wait, or be denied. Read from a project's file only in a trusted workspace.

managed_permission_rules_only.description: A session may not allow a tool for itself. Read from a project's file only in a trusted workspace.

managed_mcp_servers_only.description: A client may not offer a session its own tools. Read from a project's file only in a trusted workspace.

shell_timeout_ms.description: How long a shell command may run before it, and everything it started, is stopped.

tool_output_limit.description: Bytes of a tool's output the model sees; the rest is kept, and read_output pages it back.

tool_failures_note_at.description: Failures of one tool in a row after which the model is told to stop and reconsider; 0 never.

tool_failures_stop_at.description: Failures of one tool in a row that stop the turn and ask whether it goes on, budget or not; 0 never.

read_roots.description: Directories outside the workspace the read tools may reach. Read from a project's file only in a trusted workspace.

mcp.description: The workspace's own MCP servers, by name. Read from a project's file only in a trusted workspace.

command.description: A server on its standard streams: the program to run.

cd.description: The directory to run it in. Unset: the workspace.

url.description: A server over HTTP: its URL.

headers.description: Headers sent with every request to a server over HTTP. `{env:VAR}` reads a value from the environment.

oauth.description: A server over HTTP that wants you signed in: how to sign in.

client_id.description: A client registered in advance with the server's authorization server.

scopes.description: The scopes to ask for. Unset: what the server says it wants.

redirect_uri.description: Where the browser comes back: `http://` on 127.0.0.1, [::1] or localhost. Unset: 127.0.0.1, any free port.

resource.description: Send the resource indicator; `false` for an authorization server that refuses it.

issuer.description: The authorization server, for a server that publishes no metadata naming one.

timeout_ms.description: How long one call may take.

watch.description: Act on `AI!` and `AI?` comments in the workspace's files.

watch_debounce_ms.description: How long watch mode waits for writes to settle.

watch_poll_interval_ms.description: How often watch mode polls where it cannot be told.

fs_events.description: Record every file change in the workspace as an event.

fs_debounce_ms.description: How long file events wait for writes to settle.

default_agent.description: The agent a session starts with.

resume_on_restart.description: A session that comes back after a restart carries on by itself.

loop_max_failures.description: Failed turns in a row that stop a loop.

memory.description: Agents read the project brief, `.troupe/memory.md`, into every prompt and write it with `remember`. `/memory` shows it.

memory_auto_refresh.description: A new session in a git repository refreshes a missing or stale brief, but not within `memory_max_age_days` of a refresh that built nothing; never a headless run.

memory_max_chars.description: How much of the brief goes into a prompt.

memory_max_age_days.description: How old the brief may be before it counts as stale.

instructions_max_chars.description: How many characters of instruction files (`AGENTS.md` and its aliases, every scope together) go into a prompt; the nearest are kept whole first.

trusted_workspaces.description: Workspaces whose own files may set the keys marked trusted. A path trusts everything under it. Read only from the user's config.yaml.

state_dir.description: Where session logs go. Unset: the platform's state directory. Read from a project's file only in a trusted workspace.

fake_script.description: With `provider: fake`, the file of scripted answers. Read from a project's file only in a trusted workspace.

mouse.description: The terminal UI captures the mouse: a click activates a window and the wheel scrolls. Off keeps the terminal's own click-and-drag selection; `troupe --no-mouse` turns it off for one run.

ui.description: What follows a person from one client to the other. The daemon keeps it and acts on none of it.

theme.description: The palette the desktop app and the terminal UI draw in: `afterglow`, `signal`, `footlight` or `limelight`. One a client does not know reads as `afterglow`.

blink.description: What waits on you blinks: the terminal UI's mark and border of a window that needs you. Off holds them lit.

mode.description: Light or dark in the desktop app, or `system` to follow the computer.

notifications.description: The desktop app says when a session nobody is reading finishes a turn or waits for you.

auth_token.description: Old spelling of api_key with auth: bearer. Read from a project's file only in a trusted workspace.
